text:
Toronto has lost eight straight (a shootout loss to the Kings was the eighth, per Daily Faceoff Toronto), and the headlines around Auston Matthews have turned to where he might go. "Why trading Auston Matthews may actually be the best case for the Maple Leafs" (Hockey Patrol) and talk of the Flyers calling (NHLRumors.com) are speculation, not reported moves, but that is the conversation around the captain right now. He also took an awkward overtime fall against the Kings; Yahoo Sports reported Jim Hiller confirmed he is OK.

His own season is not the problem. Matthews has 32 points (13 goals) in 24 games, playing nearly 21 minutes a night, and he ranks seventh in the league in wins added by goals. With him on at five-on-five, Toronto takes 56% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and Evolving-Hockey had him driving play last season against 99th-percentile competition.

Some of the points are luck. His team has scored 8.7 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and his 16.9% shooting sits above his usual range. On-ice luck like that tends to fade, even when the underlying play is this good.
